messages:
acme-dev-rep: Hey team — hitting a weird issue with our streaming integration. We get a 200 and start receiving SSE lines, then mid-stream the connection closes and our client sees a 429 right after reconnect. Billing shows token usage spiking (looks like tokens counted twice). Can you help debug?

Alex: Sorry about that. Can you paste a minimal repro and the exact timestamps/IDs you see in billing? Also which SDK or client are you using?

acme-dev-rep: Repro steps below (Node EventSource polyfill). We run with a single prompt, start streaming, around 5s the stream halts, client reconnects automatically, then gets a 429 with body: `\{"error\":\"rate_limited\",\"quota_remaining\":0\}`. Billing shows ~2x the expected tokens for that request. Timestamps: request start 2026-03-14T14:00:00Z, reconnect 2026-03-14T14:00:05Z, billing entries show charges at 14:00:01 and 14:00:06. Client code: ```js
const EventSource = require('eventsource');
const es = new EventSource('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=fast-lite', {
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.RW_KEY}` }
});
es.onmessage = e => console.log('msg', e.data);
es.onerror = err => { console.log('err', err); es.close(); /* lib reconnects */ };
```

Sara: Thanks, this helps. Tagging eng-runtime. @Sara: can you check stream session handling and token accounting?

Sara: I can repro locally with a high-latency proxy. I see two distinct request IDs in our front proxy logs for that single user-visible operation: `req_01a` then `req_01b`. The second one returns a 429 because the quota check ran on reconnect. The billing pipeline consumes token deltas on each completed HTTP response and we currently treat a reconnect as a new request with no session affinity.

Mike: From billing side: our pipeline indexes each completed response and attributes tokens by request_id. If the reconnect completes another partial/complete response, it's counted again. There's no dedupe for short-lived reconnects. We do have an idempotency key feature for non-streaming requests but we don't accept idempotency headers for SSE connections right now.

acme-dev-rep: So is the root cause that a reconnect makes the platform re-emit the rest of the response, and both fragments are billed? We only want final tokens billed once.

Sara: Correct. There are two problems: 1) The runtime creates a new response object on reconnect and doesn't annotate it as a resume; 2) Billing can't tell these are the same logical session because there's no stable session id carried across reconnects.

Jen: SRE note: I pulled proxy logs and saw the TCP FIN/RESET from the client at 14:00:04, likely due to transient network issue. Our ingress treats that as a completed connection and our downstream backend flushes caches and emits the partial response. On reconnect we spin up a fresh backend request (same model shard) which resumes from the model but then produces overlapped tokens.

Alex: We need a mitigation path for customers today and a fix for platform:
- Short-term mitigation: Have clients send a custom session header (e.g., `X-RW-Stream-Session`) on initial connect and on reconnect. If the header matches the billing layer can hold off duplicate accounting for a 10s resume window. Document as experimental.
- Medium-term: Support Last-Event-ID or a server-assigned stream session id and make billing dedupe by session+offset.
- Long-term: Runtime should support resume semantics (so we don't re-run tokens already emitted) and billing should consume only deltas after resume offset.

acme-dev-rep: We can add `X-RW-Stream-Session` to our client fairly quickly. Any guidance for value? UUID per logical prompt.

Sara: That would help. Also avoid immediate client reconnect loops — add exponential backoff and include the header so we can correlate. We'll patch billing to ignore duplicate completions for the same session id within 15s as a stopgap.

Mike: On billing side I'll add a quick filter that groups events by `stream_session` if present and merges sequential token entries within a 20s window. Not perfect but should prevent double-charge for common flaps. Will push a hotfix to staging first.

deploy-bot: deploy-started: billing/hotfix/merge-session-dedupe -> staging (by Mike)

Sara: Engineering action items I'm tracking: 1) Add optional `X-RW-Stream-Session` acceptance in runtime proxy and propagate to backend. 2) Instrument response objects with `stream_session` and `offset_emitted` so billing has meaningful keys. 3) Add resume-capable path design doc to eng-runtime.

Jen: Also adding ingress change: mark connection as "transient-reset" if client FINs within 10s after opening and do not signal backend to finalize billing until 10s idle — that will reduce noise when clients have brief flaps. But careful: cannot delay billing too long for real completes.

acme-dev-rep: Appreciate the responses. Quick ask — can you confirm when the billing hotfix will be in staging and when we might see reduced duplicate billing? Our customer billing alerts fired and they are upset.

Mike: Hotfix in staging in ~30m, we'll monitor a canary and then to prod in a few hours if green. I'll DM you the deployment link and breakdown once canary runs.

Alex: For immediate support — if you can send the stream session UUID and the two request IDs from your client logs we can retroactively refund obvious double-charges while we deploy fix.

acme-dev-rep: Sending IDs via DM. Also attaching raw logs.

Sara: Repro note for eng: sample ingress log snippet showing duplicate entries: ```
2026-03-14T14:00:00.123Z ingress req_id=req_01a user=acme stream_session=abc-123 status=200 bytes=1024
2026-03-14T14:00:04.987Z ingress req_id=req_01a connection=FIN reason=client-reset
2026-03-14T14:00:05.010Z ingress req_id=req_01b user=acme stream_session=abc-123 status=206 bytes=2048
2026-03-14T14:00:05.200Z backend req_id=req_01b model=fast-lite tokens_emitted=600
```

Sara: Note `status=206` here is an internal marker for partial/resumed emit; it's not surfaced to clients. We should ensure that billing treats 206 + same session as incremental, not additive from zero.

Jen: Safety checks: ensure the resume window is configurable per org. For high-security customers they may want 0s — i.e., never collapse. We'll default to 15s.

Mike: Post-deploy plan: run a billing reconciliation job to find suspicious duplicate charges from last 24h for accounts that started streams and had reconnects in <= 20s. We'll auto-queue refunds for matches and contact customers with details.

acme-dev-rep: Thanks. One more thing — our client uses standard EventSource which doesn't expose Last-Event-ID easily. Would appreciate a pattern to attach session id in query or header.

Alex: Recommend header for now: `X-RW-Stream-Session: <uuid>`. Query param is okay but headers are less likely to be cached by intermediaries. We'll add docs to the streaming best-practices page.

Sara: Follow-up: I've started a draft PR to accept session header and propagate `stream_session` metadata. Linking in thread once ready.

deploy-bot: deploy-finished: billing/hotfix/merge-session-dedupe -> staging (status=success)

Mike: Hotfix applied to staging and canary looks clean. No duplicate billing observed for test reconnects. Planning prod push in 2h pending e2e.

Jen: We'll monitor ingress metrics (reconnect rate, short-lived connections) and billing ingestion lag. Alerting added if duplicate token delta rate > 0.5% for any org.

acme-dev-rep: Great — thanks everyone. We'll add the header and throttle client reconnects. Please ping when prod fix lands and for the refund status.

Alex: Will do. Closing loop once prod deploy completes and refunds are queued. Appreciate your patience. :thumbsup:
